Apple officially launched its latest flagship models, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, today. Although the two Pro models are largely similar, each has its own exclusive advantage.

#1: iPhone 18 Pro comes with C2 modem, while iPhone 18 Pro Max retains Qualcomm

Apple began transitioning its products to in-house cellular modems in early 2025, with the first device to feature the C1 modem being the iPhone 16e. Its successor, the C1X, was later featured in the iPhone Air released last autumn.

Now Apple has launched the next-generation C2 modem and applied it to the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, but strangely, the iPhone 18 Pro Max has not adopted it.

According to Apple's official tech specs page, the C2 and the Qualcomm modem used in the iPhone 18 Pro Max have similar specs — for example, both support mmWave in the US.

However, Apple's in-house designed modem brings several exclusive features that Pro Max users cannot enjoy.

#2: iPhone 18 Pro Max sees far greater battery life improvement than iPhone 18 Pro

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have improved battery performance this generation, but as earlier rumours suggested, Apple has reserved the biggest leap for the Pro Max model.

Here's the official battery life comparison between this year's new models and last year's:

Battery Life (video playback) iPhone 18 Pro up to 36 hours iPhone 18 Pro Max up to 45 hours iPhone 17 Pro up to 33 hours iPhone 17 Pro Max up to 39 hours

As the table above shows, the iPhone 18 Pro Max gained six additional hours of video playback, while the iPhone 18 Pro only gained three.

Nic's most upvoted comment:

I was ready to upgrade from my 12/13/16 Pro to the Max, but the lack of the Apple C2 modem is a dealbreaker. The C2 is more power-efficient and performs better in low-signal environments — the most appealing part is the "Limit Precise Location" feature, which prevents carriers from harvesting as much useful location-tracking data.

Although the Pro Max has long been the battery life champion across generations, the iPhone 18 Pro Max's lead is more pronounced than ever.
